claim: ATP synthases produce ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate with energy from a transmembrane proton motive force.
source: ATP synthases produce ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate with energy from a transmembrane proton motive force.
evidence: This is a fundamental statement about ATP synthase function that is established scientific knowledge.

claim: Bacterial ATP synthases are the simplest form of the enzyme.
source: Bacterial ATP synthases have been studied extensively because they are the simplest form of the enzyme and because of the relative ease of genetic manipulation of these complexes.
evidence: This is a comparative statement based on established knowledge about ATP synthase complexity across different organisms.

claim: The Bacillus PS3 ATP synthase was expressed in Escherichia coli.
source: We expressed the Bacillus PS3 ATP synthase in Eschericia coli, purified it, and imaged it by cryo-EM, allowing us to build atomic models of the complex in three rotational states.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: Atomic models of the Bacillus PS3 ATP synthase were built in three rotational states.
source: We expressed the Bacillus PS3 ATP synthase in Eschericia coli, purified it, and imaged it by cryo-EM, allowing us to build atomic models of the complex in three rotational states.
evidence: This describes the structural results obtained from cryo-EM analysis.

claim: The position of subunit ε shows how it is able to inhibit ATP hydrolysis while allowing ATP synthesis.
source: The position of subunit ε shows how it is able to inhibit ATP hydrolysis while allowing ATP synthesis.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation based on the structural data obtained in the study.

claim: The structures reveal the path of transmembrane proton translocation.
source: The structures reveal the path of transmembrane proton translocation and provide a model for understanding decades of biochemical analysis interrogating the roles of specific residues in the enzyme.
evidence: This describes a key finding from the structural analysis.

claim: ATP synthases are found in bacteria and chloroplasts as monomers.
source: These enzymes are found in bacteria and chloroplasts as monomers, and in mitochondria as rows of dimers that bend the inner membrane to facilitate formation of the mitochondrial cristae (Davies et al., 2012; Paumard et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: ATP synthases are found in mitochondria as rows of dimers that bend the inner membrane to facilitate formation of the mitochondrial cristae.
source: These enzymes are found in bacteria and chloroplasts as monomers, and in mitochondria as rows of dimers that bend the inner membrane to facilitate formation of the mitochondrial cristae (Davies et al., 2012; Paumard et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Davies et al., 2012 and Paumard et al., 2002.

claim: Proton translocation across the membrane-embedded FO region occurs via two offset half-channels.
source: Proton translocation across the membrane-embedded FO region of the complex occurs via two offset half-channels (Vik and Antonio, 1994; Junge et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Vik and Antonio, 1994 and Junge et al., 1997.

claim: Proton translocation in Bacillus PS3 ATP synthase may be driven by ΔpH or ΔΨ alone.
source: Studies with Bacillus PS3 ATP synthase in liposomes showed that proton translocation may be driven by ΔpH or ΔΨ alone (Soga et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Soga et al., 2012.

claim: The passage of protons causes rotation of a rotor subcomplex, inducing conformational change in the catalytic F1 region to produce ATP.
source: The passage of protons causes rotation of a rotor subcomplex, inducing conformational change in the catalytic F1 region to produce ATP (Walker, 2013) while a peripheral stalk subcomplex holds the F1 region stationary relative to the spinning rotor during catalysis.
evidence: This describes the mechanism of ATP synthesis, supported by citation to Walker, 2013.

claim: A peripheral stalk subcomplex holds the F1 region stationary relative to the spinning rotor during catalysis.
source: The passage of protons causes rotation of a rotor subcomplex, inducing conformational change in the catalytic F1 region to produce ATP (Walker, 2013) while a peripheral stalk subcomplex holds the F1 region stationary relative to the spinning rotor during catalysis.
evidence: This describes the function of the peripheral stalk, supported by citation to Walker, 2013.

claim: X-ray crystallography has been used to determine structures of the soluble F1 region of mitochondrial ATP synthase.
source: For the mitochondrial enzyme, X-ray crystallography has been used to determine structures of the soluble F1 region (Abrahams et al., 1994), partial structures of the peripheral stalk subcomplex alone (Dickson et al., 2006) and with the F1 region (Rees et al., 2009), and structures of the F1 region with the membrane-embedded ring of c-subunits attached (Stock et al., 1999; Watt et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Abrahams et al., 1994.

claim: Cryo-EM allowed the structures of the membrane-embedded FO regions from mitochondrial and chloroplast ATP synthases to be determined to near-atomic resolutions.
source: Recent breakthroughs in electron cryomicroscopy (cryo-EM) allowed the structures of the membrane-embedded FO regions from mitochondrial and chloroplast ATP synthases to be determined to near-atomic resolutions (Guo et al., 2017; Klusch et al., 2017; Srivastava et al., 2018; Hahn et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Guo et al., 2017; Klusch et al., 2017; Srivastava et al., 2018; Hahn et al., 2018.

claim: Bacterial ATP synthases have a simpler subunit composition compared to their mitochondrial counterparts.
source: Compared to their mitochondrial counterparts, bacterial ATP synthases have a simpler subunit composition.
evidence: This is a comparative statement based on established knowledge.

claim: The F1 region of bacterial ATP synthase consists of subunits α3β3γδε.
source: The F1 region consists of subunits α3β3γδε, while the FO region is usually formed by three subunits with the stoichiometry ab2c9-15.
evidence: This describes the subunit composition based on established knowledge.

claim: The FO region of bacterial ATP synthase is usually formed by three subunits with the stoichiometry ab2c9-15.
source: The F1 region consists of subunits α3β3γδε, while the FO region is usually formed by three subunits with the stoichiometry ab2c9-15.
evidence: This describes the subunit composition based on established knowledge.

claim: Chloroplasts and a few bacteria, such as Paracoccus denitrificans, possess two different but homologous copies of subunit b, named subunits b and b'.
source: Chloroplasts and a few bacteria, such as Paracoccus denitrificans, possess two different but homologous copies of subunit b, named subunits b and b' (Walker, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Walker, 2013.

claim: Each copy of subunit α and β contains a nucleotide binding site.
source: Each copy of subunit α and β contains a nucleotide binding site.
evidence: This describes a structural feature based on established knowledge.

claim: The non-catalytic α subunits each bind to a magnesium ion (Mg2+) and a nucleotide.
source: The non-catalytic α subunits each bind to a magnesium ion (Mg2+) and a nucleotide, while the catalytic β subunits can adopt different conformations and bind to Mg-ADP (βDP), Mg-ATP (βTP), or remain empty (βE).
evidence: This describes nucleotide binding properties based on established knowledge.

claim: The catalytic β subunits can adopt different conformations and bind to Mg-ADP (βDP), Mg-ATP (βTP), or remain empty (βE).
source: The non-catalytic α subunits each bind to a magnesium ion (Mg2+) and a nucleotide, while the catalytic β subunits can adopt different conformations and bind to Mg-ADP (βDP), Mg-ATP (βTP), or remain empty (βE).
evidence: This describes the conformational states of β subunits based on established knowledge.

claim: Crystal structures of bacterial F1-ATPases and c-rings from the FO regions of several species have been determined.
source: Crystal structures of bacterial F1-ATPases and c-rings from the FO regions of several species have been determined (Stocker et al., 2007; Cingolani and Duncan, 2011; Morales-Rios et al., 2015; Shirakihara et al., 2015; Ferguson et al., 2016; Pogoryelov et al., 2009; Preiss et al., 2010; Preiss et al., 2013; Preiss et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Structures of intact ATP synthases from E. coli have been determined to overall resolutions of 6 to 7 Å by cryo-EM.
source: Structures of intact ATP synthases from E. coli have been determined to overall resolutions of 6 to 7 Å by cryo-EM, with the FO region showing lower quality than the rest of the maps, presumably due to conformational flexibility (Sobti et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Sobti et al., 2016.

claim: In E. coli ATP synthase structures, the FO region shows lower quality than the rest of the maps, presumably due to conformational flexibility.
source: Structures of intact ATP synthases from E. coli have been determined to overall resolutions of 6 to 7 Å by cryo-EM, with the FO region showing lower quality than the rest of the maps, presumably due to conformational flexibility (Sobti et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the cited structural study and includes speculation about the cause.

claim: In structures of both intact ATP synthase and dissociated F1-ATPase from bacteria, subunit ε adopts an 'up' conformation that inhibits the ATP hydrolysis by the enzyme.
source: In structures of both intact ATP synthase (Sobti et al., 2016) and dissociated F1-ATPase (Cingolani and Duncan, 2011; Shirakihara et al., 2015) from bacteria, subunit ε adopts an 'up' conformation that inhibits the ATP hydrolysis by the enzyme.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Sobti et al., 2016; Cingolani and Duncan, 2011; Shirakihara et al., 2015.

claim: In Bacillus PS3, subunit ε mediated inhibition is dependent on the concentration of free ATP.
source: In the thermophilic bacterium Bacillus PS3, this subunit ε mediated inhibition is dependent on the concentration of free ATP (Kato et al., 1997; Suzuki et al., 2003; Saita et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kato et al., 1997; Suzuki et al., 2003; Saita et al., 2010.

claim: Low ATP concentrations (e.g. <0.7 mM) promote the inhibitory up conformation of subunit ε in Bacillus PS3.
source: Low ATP concentrations (e.g. <0.7 mM) promote the inhibitory up conformation while a permissive 'down' conformation can be induced by a high concentration of ATP (e.g. >1 mM).
evidence: This describes experimental observations about ATP concentration effects.

claim: A permissive 'down' conformation of subunit ε can be induced by a high concentration of ATP (e.g. >1 mM) in Bacillus PS3.
source: Low ATP concentrations (e.g. <0.7 mM) promote the inhibitory up conformation while a permissive 'down' conformation can be induced by a high concentration of ATP (e.g. >1 mM).
evidence: This describes experimental observations about ATP concentration effects.

claim: The ATP concentration-dependent mechanism would allow the Bacillus PS3 ATP synthase to run in reverse, establishing a proton motive force by ATP hydrolysis, when the ATP concentration is sufficient to do so without depleting the cell's supply of ATP.
source: This mechanism would allow the Bacillus PS3 ATP synthase to run in reverse, establishing a proton motive force by ATP hydrolysis, when the ATP concentration is sufficient to do so without depleting the cell's supply of ATP.
evidence: This is a functional interpretation based on the ATP-dependent conformational changes.

claim: In E. coli, in the absence of a sufficient proton motive force to drive ATP synthesis, inhibition of ATP hydrolysis by subunit ε persists even when the concentration of free ATP is high.
source: In E. coli, however, in the absence of a sufficient proton motive force to drive ATP synthesis, inhibition of ATP hydrolysis by subunit ε persists even when the concentration of free ATP is high (Laget and Smith, 1979; Sekiya et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Laget and Smith, 1979; Sekiya et al., 2010.

claim: The structures of Bacillus PS3 ATP synthase reached overall resolutions of 3.0, 3.0, and 3.2 Å.
source: The structures reached overall resolutions of 3.0, 3.0, and 3.2 Å (Figure 1), allowing construction of nearly complete atomic models for the entire complex.
evidence: This describes the resolution achieved in the cryo-EM study.

claim: The structures allowed construction of nearly complete atomic models for the entire Bacillus PS3 ATP synthase complex.
source: The structures reached overall resolutions of 3.0, 3.0, and 3.2 Å (Figure 1), allowing construction of nearly complete atomic models for the entire complex.
evidence: This describes the outcome of the structural analysis.

claim: The structures reveal how loops in subunit a of the bacterial enzyme fill the role of additional subunits in the FO region of the mitochondrial enzyme.
source: The structures reveal how loops in subunit a of the bacterial enzyme fill the role of additional subunits in the FO region of the mitochondrial enzyme.
evidence: This is a structural interpretation comparing bacterial and mitochondrial enzymes.

claim: The structures provide a framework for understanding decades of mutagenesis experiments designed to probe the mechanism of ATP synthases.
source: Most significantly, the structures provide a framework for understanding decades of mutagenesis experiments designed to probe the mechanism of ATP synthases.
evidence: This describes the significance of the structural data in relation to previous biochemical studies.

claim: The general architecture of the Bacillus PS3 enzyme resembles E. coli ATP synthase and the spinach chloroplast enzyme.
source: The general architecture of the enzyme resembles E. coli ATP synthase (Sobti et al., 2016) and the more distantly related spinach chloroplast enzyme (Hahn et al., 2018) but with striking differences.
evidence: This is a comparative structural observation supported by citations.

claim: The three catalytic β subunits of Bacillus PS3 adopt 'open', 'closed', and 'open' conformations.
source: As observed previously in a Bacillus PS3 F1-ATPase crystal structure (PDB 4XD7) (Shirakihara et al., 2015), the three catalytic β subunits adopt 'open', 'closed', and 'open' conformations, different from the 'half-closed', 'closed', and 'open' conformations seen in the auto-inhibited E. coli F1-ATPase (Cingolani and Duncan, 2011), and the 'closed', 'closed', and 'open' conformations seen in chloroplast ATP synthase (Hahn et al., 2018) and most mitochondrial ATP synthase structures (Abrahams et al., 1994; Stock et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Shirakihara et al., 2015 and comparison with other structures.

claim: The three catalytic β subunits of E. coli F1-ATPase adopt 'half-closed', 'closed', and 'open' conformations.
source: As observed previously in a Bacillus PS3 F1-ATPase crystal structure (PDB 4XD7) (Shirakihara et al., 2015), the three catalytic β subunits adopt 'open', 'closed', and 'open' conformations, different from the 'half-closed', 'closed', and 'open' conformations seen in the auto-inhibited E. coli F1-ATPase (Cingolani and Duncan, 2011), and the 'closed', 'closed', and 'open' conformations seen in chloroplast ATP synthase (Hahn et al., 2018) and most mitochondrial ATP synthase structures (Abrahams et al., 1994; Stock et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Cingolani and Duncan, 2011.

claim: The difference in β subunit conformations suggests species-specific differences in inhibition by subunit ε.
source: This difference, with the half-closed βDP of the E. coli enzyme appearing as open in the Bacillus PS3 enzyme, suggests species-specific differences in inhibition by subunit ε (Figure 1B, pink density), which inserts into the α/β interface and forces βDP into the open conformation.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on structural comparison.

claim: Subunit ε inserts into the α/β interface and forces βDP into the open conformation.
source: This difference, with the half-closed βDP of the E. coli enzyme appearing as open in the Bacillus PS3 enzyme, suggests species-specific differences in inhibition by subunit ε (Figure 1B, pink density), which inserts into the α/β interface and forces βDP into the open conformation.
evidence: This describes a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: Thermophilic proteins achieve stability at high temperature through mechanisms that include an increased number of ionic interactions, shorter loops between secondary structure elements, and tighter packing of hydrophobic regions.
source: Thermophilic proteins achieve stability at high temperature through mechanisms that include an increased number of ionic interactions, shorter loops between secondary structure elements, and tighter packing of hydrophobic regions (Jaenicke and Böhm, 1998; Kumar and Nussinov, 2001; Szilágyi and Závodszky, 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Jaenicke and Böhm, 1998; Kumar and Nussinov, 2001; Szilágyi and Závodszky, 2000.

claim: Comparison of F1 region subunit structures from thermophiles and mesophiles did not show clear evidence of tighter packing or shorter loops in the complexes from thermophiles.
source: Comparison of individual subunit structures from the F1 regions of ATP synthases from thermophiles (Bacillus PS3 and Caldalaklibacillus thermarum [PDB 5HKK] (Ferguson et al., 2016)) and mesophiles (E. coli [PDB 3OAA] (Cingolani and Duncan, 2011), Paracoccus denitrificans [5DN6] (Morales-Rios et al., 2015), and Spinacia oleracea chloroplast [PDB 6FKF] (Hahn et al., 2018)) did not show clear evidence of tighter packing or shorter loops in the complexes from thermophiles.
evidence: This is based on structural comparison with cited structures.

claim: There are more ionic interactions in the F1-ATPase structures from thermophiles than from mesophiles.
source: However, there are more ionic interactions in the F1-ATPase structures from thermophiles than from mesophiles, suggesting that these interactions may play a role in stabilizing the complexes.
evidence: This is based on structural comparison and includes an interpretation.

claim: Ionic interactions may play a role in stabilizing thermophilic ATP synthase complexes.
source: However, there are more ionic interactions in the F1-ATPase structures from thermophiles than from mesophiles, suggesting that these interactions may play a role in stabilizing the complexes.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the observed structural differences.

claim: One copy of subunit b in Bacillus PS3 is positioned at a location equivalent to that of the mitochondrial subunit b.
source: In the FO region, one copy of subunit b is positioned at a location equivalent to that of the mitochondrial subunit b, while the second copy occupies the position of yeast subunit 8 (mammalian A6L) on the other side of subunit a (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a structural observation comparing bacterial and mitochondrial enzymes.

claim: The second copy of subunit b in Bacillus PS3 occupies the position of yeast subunit 8 (mammalian A6L) on the other side of subunit a.
source: In the FO region, one copy of subunit b is positioned at a location equivalent to that of the mitochondrial subunit b, while the second copy occupies the position of yeast subunit 8 (mammalian A6L) on the other side of subunit a (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a structural observation comparing bacterial and mitochondrial enzymes.

claim: Bacillus PS3 ATP synthase contains 10 c-subunits.
source: Despite the different c-ring sizes (10 c-subunits in Bacillus PS3 versus 14 in spinach chloroplasts), the backbone positions of subunits ab2 from Bacillus PS3 overlap with subunits abb' from spinach chloroplast ATP synthase (Hahn et al., 2018) (Figure 1—figure supplement 5A).
evidence: This describes the c-ring stoichiometry determined from the structure.

claim: Spinach chloroplast ATP synthase contains 14 c-subunits.
source: Despite the different c-ring sizes (10 c-subunits in Bacillus PS3 versus 14 in spinach chloroplasts), the backbone positions of subunits ab2 from Bacillus PS3 overlap with subunits abb' from spinach chloroplast ATP synthase (Hahn et al., 2018) (Figure 1—figure supplement 5A).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hahn et al., 2018.

claim: The backbone positions of subunits ab2 from Bacillus PS3 overlap with subunits abb' from spinach chloroplast ATP synthase.
source: Despite the different c-ring sizes (10 c-subunits in Bacillus PS3 versus 14 in spinach chloroplasts), the backbone positions of subunits ab2 from Bacillus PS3 overlap with subunits abb' from spinach chloroplast ATP synthase (Hahn et al., 2018) (Figure 1—figure supplement 5A).
evidence: This is a structural comparison observation.

claim: Structural differences between Bacillus PS3 and E. coli FO regions in transmembrane α-helices of subunit b relative to subunit a are likely due to the lower resolution of the E. coli maps.
source: Comparison of the atomic model of the FO region from Bacillus PS3 and the backbone model of the E. coli complex from cryo-EM at ~7 Å resolution (PDB 5T4O) (Sobti et al., 2016) showed significant structural differences in transmembrane α-helices of subunit b relative to subunit a (Figure 1—figure supplement 5B). Rather than reflecting true differences between E. coli and Bacillus PS3 ATP synthase structures, these deviations are likely due to the lower resolution of the E. coli maps.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on comparison of structures at different resolutions.

claim: The most striking difference between the three rotational states of the Bacillus PS3 structure is the angular position of the rotor (subunits γεc10).
source: As expected, the most striking difference between the three rotational states of the Bacillus PS3 structure is the angular position of the rotor (subunits γεc10) (Figure 2A, Video 1).
evidence: This describes the main difference observed between the three structural states.

claim: The structure of the ATP synthase, with three αβ pairs in the F1 region and 10 c-subunits in the FO region, results in symmetry mismatch between the 120° steps of the F1 motor and 36° steps of the FO motor.
source: The structure of the ATP synthase, with three αβ pairs in the F1 region and 10 c-subunits in the FO region, results in symmetry mismatch between the 120° steps of the F1 motor and 36° steps of the FO motor.
evidence: This is a geometric inference based on the structural stoichiometry.

claim: The 120° steps of the F1 motor gives an average rotational step of 3.3 c-subunits, with the closest integer steps being 3, 4 and 3 c-subunits.
source: The 120° steps of the F1 motor gives an average rotational step of 3.3 c-subunits, with the closest integer steps being 3, 4 and 3 c-subunits.
evidence: This is a calculation based on the structural stoichiometry.

claim: The observed rotational step sizes in the three rotational states of the ATP synthase appear to be almost exactly 3, 4 and 3 c-subunits.
source: By comparing the positions of equivalent c-subunits in different rotational states, the observed rotational step sizes in the three rotational states of the ATP synthase appear to be almost exactly 3, 4 and 3 c-subunits (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is based on structural comparison of the three states.

claim: At the present resolution, the structures of subunit a and the c-ring do not appear to differ between rotary states.
source: At the present resolution, the structures of subunit a and the c-ring do not appear to differ between rotary states.
evidence: This is an observation from the structural analysis.

claim: Similar integer step sizes were found in yeast ATP synthase and V-ATPase, which also contain 10 c-subunits.
source: Similar integer step sizes were found in yeast ATP synthase (Vinothkumar et al., 2016) and V-ATPase (Zhao et al., 2015), which also contain 10 c-subunits.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Vinothkumar et al., 2016 and Zhao et al., 2015.

claim: Non-integer steps were seen in the chloroplast (14 c-subunits) and bovine (8 c-subunits) ATP synthases.
source: However, non-integer steps were seen in the chloroplast (14 c-subunits) (Hahn et al., 2018) and bovine (8 c-subunits) (Zhou et al., 2015) ATP synthases, indicating that the c-subunit steps between the rotational states of rotary ATPases likely depends on the number of c-subunits.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hahn et al., 2018 and Zhou et al., 2015.

claim: The c-subunit steps between the rotational states of rotary ATPases likely depends on the number of c-subunits.
source: However, non-integer steps were seen in the chloroplast (14 c-subunits) (Hahn et al., 2018) and bovine (8 c-subunits) (Zhou et al., 2015) ATP synthases, indicating that the c-subunit steps between the rotational states of rotary ATPases likely depends on the number of c-subunits.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of different ATP synthases.

claim: The unequal number of c-subunit steps between rotational states or the different interactions made by the three αβ pairs with the b2δ peripheral stalk could lead to a variable rotation speed for the c-ring in the active enzyme.
source: The unequal number of c-subunit steps between rotational states or the different interactions made by the three αβ pairs with the b2δ peripheral stalk could lead to a variable rotation speed for the c-ring in the active enzyme, analogous to kinetic limping in kinesin motors (Asbury et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation with analogy to kinesin motors.

claim: Flexibility in the enzyme could maintain a constant rotational velocity.
source: Alternatively, flexibility in the enzyme could maintain a constant rotational velocity.
evidence: This is a speculative alternative explanation.

claim: Flexibility is thought to be important for the smooth transmission of power between the F1 and FO regions, which often have mismatched symmetries.
source: Indeed, flexibility is thought to be important for the smooth transmission of power between the F1 and FO regions, which often have mismatched symmetries (Wang and Oster, 1998; Pänke et al., 2001; Mitome et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Wang and Oster, 1998; Pänke et al., 2001; Mitome et al., 2004.

claim: Earlier studies suggested that the central stalk (subunits γ and ε in bacteria) is the main region responsible for the transient storage of torsional energy in rotary ATPases.
source: Earlier studies suggested that the central stalk (subunits γ and ε in bacteria) is the main region responsible for the transient storage of torsional energy in rotary ATPases (Sielaff et al., 2008; Wächter et al., 2011; Ernst et al., 2012; Okazaki and Hummer, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Sielaff et al., 2008; Wächter et al., 2011; Ernst et al., 2012; Okazaki and Hummer, 2015.

claim: Comparison of the three rotational states of the Bacillus PS3 enzyme shows that C-terminal water-soluble part of subunit b displays the most significant conformational variability between states.
source: Comparison of the three rotational states of the Bacillus PS3 enzyme also shows that C-terminal water-soluble part of subunit b displays the most significant conformational variability between states, while the subunits in the F1 region show little flexibility beyond the catalytic states of the αβ pairs (Figure 2C; Video 1).
evidence: This is based on structural comparison of the three states.

claim: The subunits in the F1 region show little flexibility beyond the catalytic states of the αβ pairs.
source: Comparison of the three rotational states of the Bacillus PS3 enzyme also shows that C-terminal water-soluble part of subunit b displays the most significant conformational variability between states, while the subunits in the F1 region show little flexibility beyond the catalytic states of the αβ pairs (Figure 2C; Video 1).
evidence: This is based on structural comparison of the three states.

claim: The structure of the yeast ATP synthase FO dimer, which lacked the F1 region and an intact peripheral stalk, showed that the c-ring and subunit a are held together by hydrophobic interactions rather than by the peripheral stalk.
source: The structure of the yeast ATP synthase FO dimer (Guo et al., 2017), which lacked the the F1 region and an intact peripheral stalk, showed that the c-ring and subunit a are held together by hydrophobic interactions rather than by the peripheral stalk.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Guo et al., 2017.

claim: In Bacillus PS3 ATP synthase, the peripheral stalk is structurally simpler and more flexible than in yeast mitochondria.
source: In Bacillus PS3 ATP synthase, the peripheral stalk is structurally simpler and more flexible than in yeast mitochondria (Srivastava et al., 2018), suggesting that the bacterial subunits a and the c-ring are also held together by hydrophobic interactions and not the peripheral stalk.
evidence: This is a comparative structural observation with citation.

claim: The bacterial subunits a and the c-ring are held together by hydrophobic interactions and not the peripheral stalk.
source: In Bacillus PS3 ATP synthase, the peripheral stalk is structurally simpler and more flexible than in yeast mitochondria (Srivastava et al., 2018), suggesting that the bacterial subunits a and the c-ring are also held together by hydrophobic interactions and not the peripheral stalk.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural comparison.

claim: Additional subunits, such as those in the central stalk, may show flexibility while under strain during rotation.
source: Given that these structures represent resting states of the bacterial ATP synthase, additional subunits, such as those in the central stalk, may show flexibility while under strain during rotation.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about dynamic behavior not captured in the static structures.

claim: The structure of the F1 region of the intact Bacillus PS3 ATP synthase shows that the three catalytic β-subunits (βE, βTP, and βDP) adopt 'open', 'closed', and 'open' conformations, respectively.
source: The structure of the F1 region of the intact Bacillus PS3 ATP synthase and the earlier crystal structure of the dissociated F1-ATPase (PDB 4XD7) (Shirakihara et al., 2015) both show that the three catalytic β-subunits (βE, βTP, and βDP) adopt 'open', 'closed', and 'open' conformations, respectively (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is based on the current structural data and comparison with a crystal structure.

claim: In the Bacillus PS3 F1-ATPase crystal structure prepared in the presence of CyDTA, there was no nucleotide in the three noncatalytic sites of the three α-subunits.
source: In the crystal structure, which was prepared in the presence of CyDTA (trans-1,2-Diaminocyclohexane-N, N, N′, N′-tetraacetic acid monohydrate) as a chelating agent, there was no nucleotide in the three noncatalytic sites of the three α-subunits and the only nucleotide in a catalytic site was an ADP molecule without a Mg2+ ion in the βTP site.
evidence: This describes the nucleotide occupancy in the crystal structure.

claim: In the Bacillus PS3 F1-ATPase crystal structure, the only nucleotide in a catalytic site was an ADP molecule without a Mg2+ ion in the βTP site.
source: In the crystal structure, which was prepared in the presence of CyDTA (trans-1,2-Diaminocyclohexane-N, N, N′, N′-tetraacetic acid monohydrate) as a chelating agent, there was no nucleotide in the three noncatalytic sites of the three α-subunits and the only nucleotide in a catalytic site was an ADP molecule without a Mg2+ ion in the βTP site.
evidence: This describes the nucleotide occupancy in the crystal structure.

claim: All three non-catalytic sites in the cryo-EM structure are occupied by Mg-ATP.
source: In contrast, all three non-catalytic sites in the cryo-EM map are occupied by Mg-ATP, while a Mg-ADP molecule and a weak density tentatively assigned to phosphate are found in the βTP site and by the p-loop of βE, respectively.
evidence: This describes the nucleotide occupancy observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: A Mg-ADP molecule is found in the βTP site in the cryo-EM structure.
source: In contrast, all three non-catalytic sites in the cryo-EM map are occupied by Mg-ATP, while a Mg-ADP molecule and a weak density tentatively assigned to phosphate are found in the βTP site and by the p-loop of βE, respectively.
evidence: This describes the nucleotide occupancy observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: A weak density tentatively assigned to phosphate is found by the p-loop of βE in the cryo-EM structure.
source: In contrast, all three non-catalytic sites in the cryo-EM map are occupied by Mg-ATP, while a Mg-ADP molecule and a weak density tentatively assigned to phosphate are found in the βTP site and by the p-loop of βE, respectively.
evidence: This is a tentative assignment of density in the cryo-EM map.

claim: The presence of physiological Mg2+ ions and nucleotide occupancy in the cryo-EM map suggest that it shows a snapshot of the enzyme in the middle of its physiological catalytic cycle.
source: The presence of physiological Mg2+ ions and nucleotide occupancy (Nalin and Cross, 1982) in the cryo-EM map suggest that it shows a snapshot of the enzyme in the middle of its physiological catalytic cycle.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural data with citation support.

claim: Bacillus PS3 ATP synthase is found in a conformation that has been proposed to allow ATP synthesis while ATP hydrolysis is auto-inhibited.
source: Bacillus PS3 ATP synthase is found in a conformation that has been proposed to allow ATP synthesis while ATP hydrolysis is auto-inhibited.
evidence: This describes the functional state captured in the structure.

claim: In this state, subunit ε maintains an up conformation and inserts into the αDPβDP interface, forcing βDP to adopt an open conformation.
source: In this state, subunit ε maintains an up conformation and inserts into the αDPβDP interface, forcing βDP to adopt an open conformation (Figure 3A, lower, dashed box) (Shirakihara et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes a structural observation with citation support.

claim: In the crystal structure, the C-terminal sequence of subunit ε was modeled as two α-helical segments broken at Ser 106.

source: Overall, amino acid side chain detail can be seen for subunits α3, β3, γ, δ, ε, a, c10-ring, and the transmembrane α-helices of b2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
